learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Chose 1.6 against 2.5 and 3.4; locked it in.
observations.exploration: Pick someone selected Ana then Hub, four friends. Pick 100 more: 101 picks average 3.32, hub 78/101. Second 100: 201 picks average 3.43, hub 163/201. Population average retained 1.6.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 3.4; connected actual 3.43 mean and 163 hub selections to four leaves and one hub, 0.2 × 1 + 0.8 × 4. Stated five-person toy and connected unequal-degree network condition.
observations.visual: Actual 1257 × 936 dark screenshot inspected. Star graph labels friend counts, selected person dashed outline, hub gold and selected edge bright. Counters and explanation readable; reveal bottom extends to viewport edge.

prediction.reason: Clear numerical choice tests treating friend sample as population sample.

interaction.reason: Single selection shows path and batches reveal sampling difference.
interaction.evidence: Ana to Hub; 101 mean3.32 and 201 mean3.43.

payoff.reason: Connects actual sample counts to exact weighted mean and limits generalization.
payoff.evidence: 163/201 hub; weighted3.4; unequal counts in connected networks.

clarity.reason: Graph, selected edge and paired averages explain tested desktop path.
clarity.evidence: Actual screenshot and explicit pick status.

transfer.reason: Reusable biased friend-sampling principle with conditions, but no concrete new application.
transfer.evidence: Connected network with unequal friend counts statement.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Same-as-population prediction contradicted by repeated friend averages.

visualExplanation.reason: Star structure shows why leaves repeatedly lead to hub.
visualExplanation.evidence: Four leaf edges to gold Hub screenshot.

playfulness.reason: Repeated sampling allows observing fluctuation but structure is fixed.

practicalValue.reason: Shows concrete sampling bias in comparing friends popularity.

depth.reason: Two-stage selection, sample fluctuation and degree-condition limit.

complexity.reason: Distinguishes two sampling distributions and their weighted averages.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Follow person then friend selection and compare weighted friend count to population mean.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low; two clearly labeled sampling buttons.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: two-stage sampling and weighted mean.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: decimal averages and weighted sum.

whyCool: Repeated picks keep landing on the hub, pushing the friend average toward 3.4 while everyone average stays1.6.
caveat: Fixed extreme star network; no alternative network or fresh application tested.
missingEvidence: Alternative topology and reset not tested.
Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom/reflow and motion untested.
effort: Approximately 2 minutes of actual browser review.
